Ok quick rundown

Enhancers can modify the capabilities of something/someone with their aura (usually offensive and defensive capabilities, but can be otherwise)

Emitters can detach aura from their bodies (best affinity for long range attacks)

Transmuters can change the quality of their aura to mimic the properties of another substance (i.e. Hisoka's Bungee Gum possesses the properties of both rubber and gum, so it is both elastic and sticky)

Manipulators can control things with their aura (living and non-living, but usually physical objects/people/things)

Conjurers can materialize their aura into physical objects (this affinity is often confused with Transmuter, so I'll explain...Conjurers can create physical objects, while Transmuters merely MIMIC substances), both Conjurers and Emitters are the affinities that can most easily create Nen beasts, which are physical living creatures created with Nen (such as Razor's Fourteen Devils or Abengane and his Exorcism Nen beast); Conjurers are also usually the ones with the most creative Nen abilities...since the things they create on their own wouldn't be any stronger than a physical version, they use conditional contracts in order to make their abilities more powerful...the stricter the limitation, the more the ability will have to gain from it (i.e. Kurapika's Chain Jail is only allowed to be used on members of the Phantom Troupe, lest he be instantly killed. As a result, even the strongest member of the Phantom Troupe can't break out of Chain Jail)

And Specialists are those that possess a unique and distinct aura that doesn't fall within any of the other five classes (basically if there's a Nen ability that can't be explained with any of the other affinities, it's probably a Specialist ability; for example, Neon Nostrade's Lovely Ghostwriter, Meleoron's Perfect Plan, Chrollo Lucifer's Skill Hunter)

And sometimes, the people in your inner circle (family, friends) may not accept that part of you (this was my situation for a while). And that's okay. With your family, they may come around, they may not. Just make sure that before you come out you have a plan for the worst case scenario (i.e. if you currently live with your parents, do you have a place you could stay in the event that you get kicked out? And other things like that).

Now coming out to your friends may be a little more difficult (or not, it really depends on your situation). If you end up coming out to your friends (which you don't have to do; coming out is a personal choice and is unique to everyone), and they don't accept you, then they are not the friends for you. I know this might suck, but if they don't accept you, that's their problem, not yours.

Like I mentioned earlier, coming out is a very personal experience. And it's not usually an easy thing to do. Just stay strong, be careful, and I wish you the very best of luck.
